content_html:
Carla Hall Debuts Holiday Spiced Cider-Glazed Ham

Chef Carla Hall has released her celebrated recipe for a Spiced Cider-Glazed Ham, originally featured in Food & Wine Magazine. Designed to serve as the anchor of a holiday meal, the dish is inspired by Sunday suppers at her grandmother's house. The recipe relies on a high-quality, bone-in ham—such as a heritage-breed Berkshire ham—to enhance the meat's flavor, maintain moisture, and keep the interior tender while providing a rich foundation for future soups or bean pots.

To achieve the signature glossy finish and deep flavor profile, the recipe incorporates fresh autumn apple cider reduced with brown sugar, Dijon mustard, heartwarming spices, and a splash of bourbon. Covering the ham during the initial baking phase allows the meat to gently absorb the aromatic glaze, while uncovering it near the end creates a caramelized, golden-brown crust that is both visually striking and flavorful.

Essential Preparation Steps And Ingredients

  • Ham Selection: Starting with a 7- to 8-pound spiral-cut bone-in Berkshire ham ensures ease of carving and allows the glaze to melt deep into the layers and crevices.
  • Glaze Reduction: Fresh apple cider is simmered with brown sugar, sharp Dijon mustard, warming spices, and bourbon to build a thick, syrupy consistency with balanced sweetness and tartness.
  • Baking Technique: Baking the ham covered helps retain vital juices, while uncovering it toward the end of the total three-hour preparation time develops a mouthwatering, caramelized exterior crust.

Culinary Background And Holiday Significance

The choice of ingredients in Hall's recipe reflects traditional flavor pairings meant to elevate the natural smokiness of the pork. Berkshire hams, sourced from heritage-breed pigs, offer exceptional marbling and a concentrated, meaty flavor that distinguishes them from standard grocery store varieties. Furthermore, the inclusion of fresh apple cider captures the peak flavors of the autumn season, utilizing natural sugars and tart notes to cut through the richness of the meat.

Beyond its visual appeal on a festive white china platter, the dish bridges nostalgic family memories with practical kitchen techniques. By maximizing moisture retention through strategic covering and leveraging the depth of molasses-rich brown sugar and bourbon, home cooks can replicate a professional, centerpiece-worthy main course that highlights both heritage ingredients and expert culinary styling.
